title: Validate Binary Search Tree
prompt:
Determine if a binary tree is a valid BST: every node in a left subtree is **strictly less** than its ancestor, every node in a right subtree strictly greater — at ALL levels, not just parent-child.

**Counterexample**: `[5,4,6,null,null,3,7]` is invalid — the 3 sits in 5's right subtree but is less than 5.

Pass allowed `(min, max)` bounds down the recursion.

tests.note: Integer.MAX_VALUE as a node — bounds must be long or null

hints: Checking only `left.val < node.val < right.val` misses deep violations — you need range bounds.
Helper: `valid(node, min, max)` — node.val must be strictly inside (min, max); recurse left with (min, node.val), right with (node.val, max).
Use `long` bounds (or null-able Integers) so Integer.MIN_VALUE / MAX_VALUE node values don't break the comparison.

solution.explanation: Each node constrains its whole subtree, so the recursion narrows an allowed interval. Long bounds sidestep the edge case where a node holds Integer.MIN/MAX_VALUE. O(n) time, O(height) space.
